series_start_reason: The 2026-04-09 export is held as an archive artifact rather than a published point, per the measure-series design.
note: As-published values from committed files, not recomputed. A point's comparable_to_previous is true, false (a definition break) or "unreviewed" (a move larger than the measure's declared ordinary move, not yet reviewed). Only a true pair may be drawn as a line. The ordinary-move priors in this first slice were declared with both points already known, so they are not pre-registered; priors for measures added later are declared before their first point.

measures.question: What share of active Pennsylvania practitioners carry a PractitionerRole?
measures.source: NDH bulk export joined to NPPES taxonomy (H54)

definitions.numerator: active PA practitioners with at least one PractitionerRole
definitions.denominator: active Practitioner resources with a PA address

ordinary_move.why: Coverage had not moved more than a few points between releases before 2026-08-20.

series.comparability_reason: reviewed: PractitionerRole more than doubled in this release (3,952,445 to 10,806,327 active). Coverage reads no specialty code, so the vocabulary change cannot touch it; the rise is the directory adding roles, most of them to practitioners who already had one.

measures.notes: National role coverage is not yet a measure: no committed file carries its numerator for either release.

measures.question: What share of Endpoint resources are FHIR REST endpoints software can query?

definitions.numerator: Endpoint rows whose connectionType code is hl7-fhir-rest
definitions.denominator: all Endpoint rows in the export

ordinary_move.why: The FHIR REST subset is a small, slow-moving share of a large Direct-address population.

measures.notes: The denominator is rows, not distinct endpoints. April repeated each endpoint about four times; May and August are close to one row per address.

measures.question: What share of FHIR REST endpoints resolve to a managing organization?

definitions.numerator: FHIR REST endpoints whose managingOrganization reference resolves to an Organization in the export

ordinary_move.why: Attribution depends on CMS populating one reference; a move over five points would be a change in how the export is built.

measures.question: Of the FHIR REST endpoints the NDH cannot attribute, what share do public EHR vendor files name?
measures.source: NDH bulk export plus eight public vendor endpoint files fetched at run time (H51)

definitions.numerator: unattributed FHIR REST endpoints whose base URL a vendor file maps to an organization
definitions.denominator: FHIR REST endpoints with no resolvable managingOrganization

ordinary_move.why: Both inputs change: the NDH by release and the vendor files whenever vendors republish.

series.comparability_reason: moved 0.1099 against a declared ordinary move of 0.05 (absolute); not yet reviewed

measures.notes: This measure has two clocks. The vendor files are fetched when the script runs, not when CMS releases, so a move can come from either side.

measures.question: What share of FHIR REST endpoints are payer provider directories?

definitions.numerator: FHIR REST endpoints identified as a payer provider directory

ordinary_move.why: Payer directories are a handful of endpoints in a population of about 110,000.

measures.notes: Payer organizations with an endpoint is not yet a measure: the 2026-05-08 release had no payer organization type, and the 2026-08-20 count of payer organizations carrying an endpoint is stated only in prose.

measures.question: How many Practitioner resources expose a Social Security Number?

definitions.numerator: Practitioner resources whose JSON matches the dashed SSN pattern after false-positive filtering
definitions.note: Undashed nine-digit values are out of scope; they collide with EINs and account identifiers.

ordinary_move.why: A count this small moves in large proportions on any change.

series.zero_control: asserted in source notes, not yet a structured field: The zero is checked, not assumed: 7,371,126 of 7,373,232 Practitioner resources still carry the qualification array those exposures were found in, so the scan is reading the right field
series.comparability_reason: reviewed: Remediation, not an empty query: the source records that 7,371,126 of 7,373,232 Practitioner resources still carry the qualification array the exposures were found in.

measures.question: What share of NPIs in the export fail structural or check-digit validation?

definitions.numerator: NPIs that are not ten digits or fail the Luhn check digit
definitions.denominator: NPIs carried on Practitioner and Organization resources

ordinary_move.why: CMS validates NPIs at enumeration; failures are a few records in ten million.

definitions.numerator: Practitioner-to-Role pairs whose Role specialty (CMS Medicare code) maps to the qualification NUCC code through the CMS Medicare-to-NUCC crosswalk
definitions.denominator: Practitioner-to-Role pairs where both carry a specialty

definitions.numerator: Practitioner-to-Role pairs where any Role specialty NUCC code equals any qualification NUCC code
definitions.denominator: Practitioner-to-Role pairs where both carry a specialty
definitions.note: Reads every entry of both repeating elements.

ordinary_move.why: Agreement between two fields of the same record should be stable.

breaks.reason: PractitionerRole.specialty moved from CMS Medicare codes to NUCC taxonomy codes, so definition 1 measured a lossy Medicare-to-NUCC crosswalk rather than disagreement. Definition 2 compares NUCC to NUCC.

restatements.reason: First published reading only the first entry of each repeating specialty element; restated on 2026-08-28 (e029518) to read every entry.

series.comparability_reason: definition break: PractitionerRole.specialty moved from CMS Medicare codes to NUCC taxonomy codes, so definition 1 measured a lossy Medicare-to-NUCC crosswalk rather than disagreement. Definition 2 compares NUCC to NUCC.

measures.question: What share of active practitioners can be associated with a phone number through FHIR?

definitions.numerator: active practitioners with a phone on Practitioner.telecom, PractitionerRole.telecom or a referenced Location.telecom

ordinary_move.why: Coverage sits near 100% on the Practitioner record alone.

measures.question: What share of Organization resources carry a coded type rather than free text or nothing?

definitions.numerator: Organization rows whose type carries a coding (prov, team, govt, pay and any later code)
definitions.denominator: all Organization rows in the export
definitions.note: Tax-entity (ein) and network (ntwk) records carry the type as text and count against the measure.

ordinary_move.why: Organization typing is a property of how CMS builds the export and was not expected to move.

series.comparability_reason: moved 0.08538 against a declared ordinary move of 0.05 (absolute); not yet reviewed

excluded_candidates.reason: No committed file carries the national count of practitioners with a role for either release; only rounded percentages appear, in prose. Needs the BigQuery measure pass.
2026-05-08 appears only in prose. 2026-08-20 appears in primer-scoreboard.json as a percentage plus a prose detail string, with no numerator or denominator field.
The 2026-05-08 release had no payer organization type, so its denominator does not exist; the 2026-08-20 numerator is stated only in prose.
ndh-column-coverage.json carries a rounded percentage and a row count but no numerator, and covers 2026-08-20 only. A count back-computed from a rounded percentage would be invented.
